fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. A skin disease is in the LORD's command to Moses (Numbers 5:2). A bodily discharge and being defiled by a dead body ride in the same verse, so that one verse holds three groups. Short verse, big list, and you spotted the one this card was after.

Owing a debt sounds like camp trouble, friend, but the command doesn't cover it. The LORD's list is a skin disease, a bodily discharge, and being defiled by a dead body (Numbers 5:2). Money never comes up in that verse. Check your pockets all you want, nobody's asking for them here.

I see why outsiders come to mind, but birthplace never comes up. Verse 2 is about a skin disease, a bodily discharge, and being defiled by a dead body. Verse 3 adds, "You must send away male and female alike…" (Numbers 5:3) Nothing in the passage sorts people by where they were born.

That's the reason, baker. The LORD says to send them outside "…so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." (Numbers 5:3) Look at where the weight falls. It's the camp, and it's the fact that He dwells right there among them. The whole command is built around that.

Priests show up later in the passage, so it's a fair guess. But the verse names the LORD: the person "…acts unfaithfully against the LORD by committing any sin against another…" (Numbers 5:6) The one wronged is just "another," and the verse doesn't say who that is. The blank wants the LORD.

Yes, baker. The guilty person "…must confess the sin he has committed." (Numbers 5:7) Confession comes first, and the making right follows in the same verse. Owning up is hard. I once blamed a missing batch of dough on the dust, and the dust never confessed either.

Not quite, baker. The text says that if there is no relative, "…the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest…" (Numbers 5:8) The guilty person doesn't keep it. It goes to the priest, and it comes with the ram of atonement.
